name: Comparative Biology PhD Program (Richard Gilder Graduate School)
detailsNote: Official information available. How students are admitted is not shown: applicants need a faculty sponsor, found through contact with faculty or assigned by the school, but the page does not describe rotations or a lab-versus-program model. Stipend amount and whether funding covers international students are not stated.
summary: PhD in comparative biology at the American Museum of Natural History's Richard Gilder Graduate School, with a 2:1 faculty-to-student ratio. Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact a faculty member before applying.

deadlines.label: Application deadline
deadlines.note: The program page lists "Deadline: December 15, 2026, 11:59 pm, ET".

timeline.interviews: Final candidates will be invited to the Richard Gilder Graduate School for interviews, whenever possible.

english.toefl: 100 or higher (iBT, typically 25 or more on each subsection) or 600 or higher (paper-based, typically 60 or more on each subsection)
english.note: TOEFL or IELTS (Academic) is required for non-native English speakers, with scores from within the past 2 years. Applicants with a degree taught in English are exempt. Scores are as the page states them, without conversion between TOEFL scales.

applicationFee.note: Request a waiver by email if the fee is a substantial financial burden; you cannot submit until it is approved. The page does not say whether international applicants qualify, so confirm.

documents: Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science (or equivalent accredited degree)
Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions, sent in sealed envelopes
A faculty sponsor, through student contact or assigned by the school
requirements.note: The school has eliminated the GRE: it will not accept GRE scores or consider them. Letters are from instructors, research advisors or other mentors.

funding.note: The page lists full tuition, stipend, research budget and health insurance among the resources, without an amount, a year, or a statement about international students.

international.note: Non-native English speakers submit TOEFL or IELTS scores.

sources.label: AMNH Richard Gilder Graduate School: Comparative Biology Ph.D. Program
